# Erdős Problem 259

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/259](https://www.erdosproblems.com/259)
-/

open scoped ArithmeticFunction.Moebius

namespace Erdos259

/--
Is $\sum_{n} \mu(n)^2\frac{n}{2^n}$ irrational?

This is true, and was proved by Chen and Ruzsa.

[ChRu99] Chen, Yong-Gao and Ruzsa, Imre Z., On the irrationality of certain series. Period. Math. Hungar. (1999), 31--37.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ster-oc/c7429943f6b3a634797dc8b2a3b01f2d/raw/8c6b5b7f08021f0aed2312542dd2e9ee7beaa6d6/Erdos259.lean"]
theorem erdos_259 : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (μ n) ^ 2 * n / (2 ^ n)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos259

reformulations.difference: Relative to the squarefree-indexed formulation in OEIS A371134 and the original Erdős problem, Lean sums over all natural numbers with Möbius-square weights, including n = 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Mathlib's Möbius square is exactly the squarefree indicator. Thus the summand equals n/2^n for squarefree n and zero otherwise. Zero is not squarefree, and the n = 0 summand vanishes. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, I proved equality with the positive-indexed sum and with the squarefree-subtype sum, including the corresponding Irrational ↔ statement. I also independently proved summability by comparison with ∑ n/2^n, so tsum's default value is not involved.

review.notes: No mathematical defect found in the sole declaration. Elaboration confirms real arithmetic throughout the summand; small-input tests for n = 0 through 15 agree with the intended series. The source database records #259 as 'proved (Lean)', and OEIS credits Chen–Ruzsa (1999), matching the file's status and positive conclusion. Access limitations: the direct Erdős webpage returned a Cloudflare challenge, and Springer exposed only the abstract; the exact formula was corroborated through the explicitly linked OEIS entry and original Erdős paper. The cited external proof has an equivalent conclusion (verified in Lean) and no explicit sorry or custom axioms. Its independent compilation encounters compatibility errors under the sandbox's Lean/Mathlib v4.33.1, so I did not certify the external proof itself; this is not evidence of a mathematical or status defect.
